findings.action: Regression from the R4 branch: inside the section, a marker line that reads as a heading once comments are removed (indented 1-3 spaces, or with a leading comment) closes the section silently. "- L1: ... a shim covers it" followed by "  # of cases on Linux <!-- note --> only." or "<!-- c --> # only on Linux." seals L1 cut with no problem, and a later L2 is dropped silently. The base engine refused the section in each case. Breaks origin R1/R2/D1 and the manual text added by R5.

R4 requires refusal messages bounded in number and size; only the number is bounded. quoteLedgerText does not truncate, so 25 prose lines of 100000 bytes give 21 problems totalling 2001842 bytes, which flow into plan warnings and lint output. A long limit id is also echoed whole (100074 bytes).

R6 changed the writer but PreflightReviewAttestation still returns nil for non-approving decisions: attest without --apply of a changes-requested within-limit of unsealed L9 prints review_attestation.plan=record and exits 0, and --apply then refuses it; the MCP preview takes the same function, so verify_blockers is empty. This breaks the rule that preview and write cannot disagree. The comments at 3162 and 3189 and the typed error text ("reject this approval", line 3147) are also stale for this case.
R1 gaps: a heading "### Accepted --> limits" (stray close marker) or a comment opened in the heading words and closed on the next line yields no limits and no problem.
R3 gap: indent counts characters, so a tab-indented (or two spaces plus tab) code block of backticks still opens a fence that silently hides a later accepted limits section.

R3 side effect: a fence nested in a list item at four spaces is no longer a fence, so a comment opener shown inside it now refuses every limit as unterminated, where the base engine sealed them. It fails closed and visibly, but no decision records the changed answer.

The stated technical risk is false: a code span continued over two lines whose second line holds a comment opener, closed by a later comment closer, hides the accepted limits section with no limit and no problem. The base engine behaves the same.
Stale doc comments: htmlCommentStart still describes the odd-backtick-count rule that R2 replaced, and line 256 refers to the removed acceptedLimitsOf.
